messages:
ash: Quick spike notes: exploring a BGP-over-VPN delegation option for Private CP customers who want deterministic egress IPs and faster route convergence than per-tenant peering. Idea: use customermanaged VGW/Transit+VGW with dynamic BGP sessions from our regional relays.

mina: Interesting. How would this differ from current peering model?

ash: Current model: per-tenant peering or TGW attachments, route propagation via cloud control plane. Problem cases: cross-account peering scale, slow propagation, and complex customer firewall allowlist workflows. BGP approach: establish a BGP session into the customer's VPN/edge and advertise per-tenant prefixes we own (or ask customer to advertise tenant subnets). That gives faster convergence and more explicit control.

garrett: Two immediate concerns: security/authorization for accepting routes, and who owns the advertised prefixes. We can't orphan customer prefixes. Also, many customers won't allow us to inject routes unless audited.

security: We'll need strict route filtering, signed route-policy, and an attestation flow. Suggest requirement: customers must create an RBAC entry in their edge to accept routes only from a known AS number list + per-prefix ACLs. Also log all route changes to KMS-backed audit trail.

mina: Operationally: what about failover? If our relay withdraws a prefix during rotation, customer might see a transient blackhole. Does BGP converge faster than peering propagation? Usually yes, but requires tuned timers: hold-time, keepalives, dampening.

ash: Exactly. We can tune timers aggressively for our sessions (e.g., keepalive 5s, hold 15s) to get sub-second detection, but that increases risk of flap sensitivity. We should experiment.

garrett: How do we prevent route hijack? If an attacker advertises same prefix, the customer could accept it. Need mutual auth. We can use TCP-AO or MD5 on BGP sessions, and validate origin with RPKI where possible, but many on-prem devices don't support RPKI. Add out-of-band controller handshake to verify peer identity before accepting routes.

security: Also require an approval step: operator-initiated cert exchange that proves controlplane ownership of the prefix. For hosted customers we can issue ephemeral attest certs; for private customer-managed edges, require them to paste a nonce in their edge config to prove control. Document this in onboarding.

mina: Implementation sketches: 1) relay BGP listener accepting sessions over VPN endpoints, 2) per-tenant prefix assignment model: either "provider-advertised" (we own small /32 or /28s) or "customer-advertised" (customer keeps origin but we coordinate), 3) controller UI to show BGP session health + route origination.

ash: Provider-advertised model is simpler for allowlist customers: they can add our small egress IP(s) to their firewall. We must avoid hoarding IPv4; use /32s from a shared pool with NAT where needed, or prefer IPv6 allocations if customers accept.

garrett: Pool management is key. Use LRU sticky assignments and reclamation TTLs similar to ENI pool idea, and export metrics: active_adverts, advert_churn, bfd_flap_rate. Add alert if churn > threshold.

neteng-bot: neteng-bot: Proposed alert: "bgp_advert_churn_high" when advert_churn > 0.05 over 5m. Pager: eng-oncall + neteng.

mina: Testing: PoC with 3 tenant edge devices (one AWS VGW, one on-prem router, one appliance) and measure failover time for withdraw/announce. Validate that keepalive tuning gives expected detection. Also test with simulated intermittent link flaps to assess dampening thresholds.

ash: Policy note: Private deployments vs Hosted: For Private CP (customer-managed controlplane), customers may run relays in their VPC and own BGP sessions themselves; we should provide a reference implementation but not own their sessions. For Hosted CP we can offer BGP as an opt-in path with strict onboarding checks.

garrett: Need to add legal/contract language for route origination responsibilities. Also include per-tenant opt-out and an automatic revert-to-peering path if BGP session fails for > 2m. Revert triggers: withdraw route and cutover to existing peering/TGW fallback.

security: Add requirement: every BGP session must be tied to a controller snapshot_id and signed by controller KMS. Logs must contain session_id, controller_snapshot, and nonce. We'll also expose these in Console for customers to audit.

mina: UX: Console should show live prefix map and allow one-click rotate of provider-assigned egress IPs. Also a red banner if session_health < 0.9. Include a CLI snippet for triage.

ash: Example BGP config we used during the PoC (on customer edge):

```
router bgp 65010
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 64513
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 password <md5-secret>
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 timers 5 15
  network 198.51.100.128/32
```

garrett: Docs & legal aside aside, implementation tasks: 1) PoC for VGW + on-prem + appliance, 2) controller/session handshake + attestation flow, 3) prefix pool manager + reclamation policy, 4) Console UI + metrics, 5) rollback/fallback path to peering/TGW, 6) security audits + legal addendum.

mina: Timeline: PoC this sprint, bench tests next sprint, RFC if PoC looks good. Who volunteers to draft RFC? I'll take the PoC checklist and test harness. Ash will draft initial RFC.

ash: I'll start RFC draft: "bgp-vpn-delegation-private-cp" and include sequence diagrams + sample configs. Tagging neteng + security + legal.

neteng-bot: neteng-bot: Runbook note created: "bgp-delegation-onboard-checklist". Reference: 1768889999.
